slides.title: Core Principles of OOP
content: OOP is based on four main principles: Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, Abstraction
These principles help in designing flexible and reusable software
They model real-world entities effectively
They improve maintainability and scalability of code

slides.title: What is Polymorphism
content: Polymorphism means 'many forms'
A single method or object behaves differently in different situations
It allows flexibility and dynamic behavior in programs
Example: same method name performing different tasks

slides.title: Types of Polymorphism
content: Compile-Time Polymorphism (Static Binding)
Run-Time Polymorphism (Dynamic Binding)
Both allow same method name but different behavior
Difference lies in when method is resolved

slides.title: Compile-Time Polymorphism
content: Method call is resolved during compilation
Achieved using method overloading
Same method name but different parameters
Example: add(int, int) and add(double, double)

slides.title: Method Overloading Rules
content: Methods must have same name but different parameters
Parameter difference can be type, number, or order
Return type alone cannot differentiate methods
Occurs within the same class

slides.title: Advantages of Compile-Time Polymorphism
content: Faster execution due to early binding
Improves readability using same method name
Helps in code reuse
Resolved at compile-time

slides.title: Run-Time Polymorphism
content: Method call is resolved during runtime
Achieved using method overriding
Based on actual object type, not reference type
Uses dynamic method dispatch

slides.title: Method Overriding Rules
content: Method must have same name, parameters, and return type
Requires inheritance (parent-child relationship)
Child class provides specific implementation
Access modifier cannot be more restrictive

slides.title: Dynamic Method Dispatch
content: JVM decides which method to call at runtime
Depends on object type, not reference type
Enables flexible and extensible code
Example: Animal reference → Dog object calls Dog method

slides.title: Compile-Time vs Run-Time Polymorphism
content: Compile-time uses method overloading, runtime uses overriding
Compile-time is faster, runtime is slightly slower
Compile-time resolved by compiler, runtime by JVM
Runtime provides more flexibility

slides.title: Encapsulation
content: Encapsulation means hiding internal data and exposing only necessary methods
Data and methods are bundled into a class
Attributes are kept private for security
Access is provided through public methods

slides.title: Benefits of Encapsulation
content: Protects sensitive data from unauthorized access
Improves code maintainability
Allows controlled modification of data
Reduces complexity by hiding implementation details

slides.title: Access Modifiers
content: Define visibility of variables and methods
Public: accessible everywhere
Private: accessible only within class
Protected and Default provide controlled access

slides.title: Inheritance
content: Inheritance allows one class to acquire properties of another
Parent class is superclass, child is subclass
Promotes code reuse and hierarchy
Example: Animal → Dog

slides.title: Types of Inheritance
content: Single Inheritance: one parent, one child
Multilevel Inheritance: chain of inheritance
Hierarchical Inheritance: one parent, multiple children
Multiple inheritance not supported in Java using classes

slides.title: Advantages of Inheritance
content: Reusability of existing code
Improves code organization
Supports extensibility
Reduces redundancy

slides.title: Method Overloading vs Overriding
content: Overloading: same class, different parameters
Overriding: parent-child classes, same method signature
Overloading resolved at compile-time
Overriding resolved at runtime

slides.title: Super Keyword
content: Used to access parent class members
Can call parent class constructor
Helps avoid ambiguity in inheritance
Used when child and parent have same variable names

slides.title: Multiple Inheritance & Diamond Problem
content: Multiple inheritance means inheriting from multiple classes
Java does not support it for classes
Diamond problem causes ambiguity in method resolution
Java solves it using interfaces

slides.title: Real-Life Example of Polymorphism
content: Animal class with method sound()
Dog overrides sound() → barks
Cat overrides sound() → meows
Same method behaves differently for each object

slides.title: Summary of Core Principles
content: Encapsulation ensures data security
Inheritance enables code reuse
Polymorphism provides flexibility
Together they form the foundation of OOP
